subject: How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles
posts:
GM's CarBravo platform aims to steer used car shoppers toward dealership networks and new vehicle sales.
Evidence: Dealer portals, trade-in data, executive statements
#Automotive #Business

Automakers say certified pre-owned programs and digital portals give used car shoppers seamless access to inventory and dealer service.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

In reality, automakers leverage used car trade-ins as a strategic funnel to compete with online retailers and upsell buyers into new cars.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.4, +0.5) — Constructive Utility

Verdict: PASS — Small Fall from Grace.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.2, z: 2)

- General Motors: PASS (0.5, 0.5) — Revamps digital portals to capture trade-in volume.
- Car Shoppers: PASS (0.4, 0.5) — Gains transparent vehicle inspection and service access.
With online retailers capturing market share, legacy automakers are modernizing certified pre-owned programs to bring buyers back into physical dealerships.

The Bright Side:
Consumers gain transparent vehicle inspections, warranty guarantees, and reliable access to local dealer maintenance networks.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing standard commercial competition (WHAT) with consumer exploitation (WHO). CarBravo is a market strategy, not a deceptive trap.

Social Physics Analysis:
GM uses transparent digital tools to address competitive friction in the retail market, aligning corporate revenue goals with buyer access in a smart cooperative loop.

The Trajectory: The Path of Small Fall from Grace.
When corporate strategy meets consumer demand through transparent platforms, it plots a steady vector toward mutual utility.

The Unavoidable Truth: Used car trade-ins are a highly lucrative gateway to new vehicle sales.

The Unavoidable Lie: Digital used car portals operate entirely independently of dealership profit motives.

Alethekanon:
GM's digital pivot is a textbook market adaptation designed to recapture trade-in value without deceptive pretexts.

Awwthekanon:
It's nice when car shopping gets a bit more transparent, giving folks reliable warranties and service options right in their hometown.

Brothekanon:
Smart move by GM. They saw Carvana eating their lunch and built an online portal so dealers can actually compete for trade-ins.

Spirithekanon:
"We join spokes in a wheel, but it is the hole in the center that makes it useful." Tao Te Ching 11 PASS
Balancing commercial utility with consumer access creates functional market harmony.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
How GM is trying to talk used car shoppers into buying new vehicles

Automakers say that substantial shares of the customers walking into a dealership looking for certified used cars end up buying new. Here's how it works.

Actual Article Body:
In this article

Affordability challenges are pushing some buyers out of the new vehicle market. Many are choosing used cars instead.

In turn, automakers are looking for ways to compete with many of the online retailers grabbing market share in the used car market and trying to bring some of those customers back into a new vehicle.

New vehicle sales tend to be more profitable for automakers, but reselling trade-ins as used vehicles is highly profitable for dealers. Used car prices are relatively strong, but newer online retailers such as Carvana and CarMax have made the market more competitive for dealers and other incumbent used car sellers.

"The internet and technology and apps on our phone have changed every aspect of retail, and probably one of the slowest areas of retail to have adopted to online and digital shopping has been the auto industry," said Ivan Feinseth, partner, chief investment officer and director of research at Tigress Financial Partners.

General Motors is a key example of automakers' attempts to address this shifting market. The automaker has revamped its certified used vehicle program, which now operates under the CarBravo name. It's essentially an online portal through which Chevrolet, Buick and GMC dealers can list their certified used vehicles and make them available to customers all over the U.S.

About 1,615 of GM's 3,700 dealers are enrolled in the program, according to the company. The only GM brand not involved is Cadillac, which maintains its own program.

"Certified" used or "preowned" vehicles are used cars that have undergone a thorough inspection and reconditioning. They typically come with guarantees and warranties from the manufacturer.

Many automakers have certified used programs for their own cars. But GM, as part of its revamp, is using CarBravo to certify vehicles made by other automakers. A lot of those cars arrive at dealerships as trade-ins, and often dealers will sell them to wholesale auctions, said John Fitzpatrick, senior manager of the CarBravo program.

"Wholesaling doesn't bring nearly the revenue that selling it to a new customer does," he said.

GM has said it is planning to net about 250,000 sales in its CarBravo program in 2026. Fitzpatrick said he doesn't expect that even half of those will end up being new car sales.

But through CarBravo, the customer gets access to GM's dealership network for service, something Fitzpatrick says is a key differentiator between its program and growing online...
